The '''2011–12 season''' was the [[List of Real Madrid C.F. seasons|108th season]] in '''[[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]''''s history and their 81st consecutive season in [[La Liga]], the top division of [[Football in Spain|Spanish football]]. It covered a period from 1 July 2011 to 30 June 2012.

Real Madrid began the season finishing runners-up in the [[2011 Supercopa de España|Supercopa de España]] to [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], losing 5–4 on aggregate. The team then went on to produce a magnificent season, winning a record 32nd [[2011–12 La Liga|La Liga]] title and setting a number of [[La Liga records and statistics|league records]], including 100 points amassed in a single season, a total of 121 goals scored, a goal difference of +89, 16 away games won, and 32 wins overall.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://msn.foxsports.com/foxsoccer/laliga/story/jose-mourinho-real-madrid-earn-vindication-after-la-liga-conquest-051312 |title=Jose Mourinho, Real Madrid earn vindication after La Liga conquest |publisher=Msn.foxsports.com |date=13 May 2012 |access-date=19 August 2012}}</ref> They also competed in the [[2011–12 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] for the 15th successive season,<ref>{{cite web|title=UEFA Champions League 2011/12 season matchweek stats pack Matchweek 1 13/09/2011 – 14/09/2011|url=http://www.uefa.com/printoutfiles/competitions/ucl/2012/e/e_01_md.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120111044512/http://www.uefa.com/printoutfiles/competitions/ucl/2012/e/e_01_md.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-date=11 January 2012|publisher=[[UEFA]]|date=9 September 2011|access-date=11 September 2011 }}</ref> losing in the semi-finals to [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] on [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalties]] (after a 3–3 aggregate tie) in heartbreaking fashion. Madrid entered the [[2011–12 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]] as the [[2010–11 Copa del Rey|defending champions]], but lost 3–4 on aggregate in the quarter-finals to Barcelona. In the same season, [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] became the fastest player to reach 100 goals scored in Spanish league history. In reaching 101 goals in 92 games, Ronaldo surpassed Real Madrid legend [[Ferenc Puskás]], who scored 100 goals in 105 matches. Ronaldo set a new club mark for individual goals scored in one year (60) and became the first player ever to score against all 19 opposition teams in a single season.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17502825 |title=Cristiano Ronaldo is fastest La Liga player to 100 goals |work=BBC Sport |date=24 March 2012 |access-date=19 August 2012}}</ref>

The season has been often termed by some newspapers as "''La Liga de los Récords''" (Spanish for "The League of the Records") as Real Madrid broke several long-standing La Liga records, the most prominent being the highest number of points in a single La Liga season. Their total of 100 was one point better than the previous record set by Barcelona in the [[2009–10 La Liga|2009–10 season]]. Real Madrid also recorded the most goals in a league season with 121, surpassing the previous record held by the Real Madrid side that scored 107 goals during the [[1989–90 La Liga|1989–90 season]].

web|title=El Real Madrid se adjudica el World Football Challenge 2011|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zCnsI8QJX9M|last=Jouve|first=Nacho|publisher=[[Real Madrid TV]]|date=1 August 2011|access-date=1 August 2011|language=es }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=2011 World Football Challenge Standings |url=http://www.mlssoccer.com/wfc/standings |publisher=[[Major League Soccer|MLSsoccer.com]] |access-date=6 August 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110811073323/http://www.mlssoccer.com/wfc/standings |archive-date=11 August 2011 }}</ref> Ronaldo finished as the [[2011 World Football Challenge#Top goalscorers|tournament's top scorer]] with four goals.<ref>{{cite web|title=World Football Challenge Stats: Top Goal Scorers – 2011/12|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/stats/scorers/_/league/global.world_football_challenge/world-football-challenge?cc=5901|publisher=[[ESPNsoccernet]]|access-date=9 September 2011|archive-date=2 November 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121102082613/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/stats/scorers/_/league/global.world_football_challenge/world-football-challenge?cc=5901|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Real Madrid started the European leg of their pre-season world tour with a triumph over newly promoted [[Bundesliga]] team [[Hertha BSC]] on 27 July in front of a sold out [[Olympic Stadium (Berlin)|Olympiastadion]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=Benzema scores 2 as Real Madrid beats Hertha |url=http://www.ctpost.com/sports/article/Benzema-scores-2-as-Real-Madrid-beats-Hertha-1614187.php |agency=[[The Associated Press]] |work=Connecticut Post|date=27 July 2011 |access-date=9 September 2011 }} {{dead link|date=June 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> [[Patrick Ebert]] opened the scoring for Hertha, but Ronaldo equalized from a long-range [[direct free kick|free kick]] and Benzema added two goals for a 3–1 victory.<ref>{{cite news|title=GOALS: Hertha Berlin 1–3 Real Madrid|last=Jones|first=Rhiannon|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xYiORsmW-JA|publisher=[[Real Madrid TV]]|date=28 July 2011|access-date=28 July 2011}}</ref> Three days later Real Madrid defeated [[Football League Championship|Championship]] side [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] 2–1 to win the [[Npower (UK)|npower]] Challenge Cup.<ref name="Report: City 1 Real Madrid 2">{{cite web|title=Report: City 1 Real Madrid 2 |url=http://www.lcfc.com/page/LatestNews/0,,10274~2406145,00.html |publisher=[[Leicester City F.C.|LCFC.com]] |date=30 July 2011 |access-date=30 July 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110920222324/http://www.lcfc.com/page/LatestNews/0%2C%2C10274~2406145%2C00.html |archive-date=20 September 2011 }}</ref> Callejón scored the opening goal and Benzema converted a rebound following a shot off the goalpost by [[Marcelo (footballer, born 1988)|Marcelo]] before [[Lloyd Dyer]] added a late consolation goal.<ref>{{cite web|title=1–2: Callejón y Benzema dan la quinta victoria|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/1330063539785/noticia/Cronica/1-2:_Callejon_y_Benzema_dan_la_quinta_victoria.htm|last=Porrero|first=Fernando|publisher=[[Real Madrid C.F.]]|date=30 July 2011|access-date=11 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121010075744/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/1330063539785/noticia/Cronica/1-2:_Callejon_y_Benzema_dan_la_quinta_victoria.htm|archive-date=10 October 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

[[José Mourinho]]'s five-game touchline ban in the [[UEFA Champions League]] due to accusatory statements following the first leg of the [[2010–11 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Semi-finals|previous season's Champions League semi-final]] was partially upheld following an appeal to [[UEFA]] on 29 July.<ref name="Mourinho appeal partially admitted">{{cite web|title=Mourinho appeal partially admitted|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/01f3-0e790c4eaf4e-e00b52e00bd0-1000--mourinho-appeal-partially-admitted/|publisher=UEFA|date=29 July 2011|access-date=29 July 2011 }}</ref> He was originally suspended for five matches, with the final game suspended for a probational period of three years, and fined €50,000<ref>{{cite web|title=Sanctions for Madrid and Barcelona |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/01f1-0e78522fbfac-66a5ae739fac-1000--sanctions-for-madrid-and-barcelona/ |publisher=UEFA |date=6 May 2011 |access-date=29 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110722010126/http://www.uefa.com/uefa/footballfirst/matchorganisation/disciplinary/news/newsid%3D1628218.html |archive-date=22 July 2011 |url-status=live }}</ref> for accusing [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] of receiving favorable treatment from UEFA and for severely criticizing German referee [[Wolfgang Stark]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Barcelona study Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho's comments with view to launching Uefa complaint|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/competitions/champions-league/8479584/Barcelona-study-Real-Madrid-manager-Jose-Mourinhos-comments-with-view-to-launching-Uefa-complaint.html|work=The Daily Telegraph|date=28 April 2011|access-date=29 July 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110712103842/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/competitions/champions-league/8479584/Barcelona-study-Real-Madrid-manager-Jose-Mourinhos-comments-with-view-to-launching-Uefa-complaint.html|archive-date=12 July 2011|url-status=live}}</ref> After serving the first game of his suspension in the second leg, Mourinho had the remaining four matches of his ban reduced to a two-game suspension with a potential two further games over a three-year probationary period.<ref>{{cite news|title=Real Madrid's Mourinho Has UEFA Suspension Modified on Appeal|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/2011-07-29/real-madrid-s-mourinho-has-uefa-suspension-modified-on-appeal.html|last=Bensch|first=Bob|publisher=[[Bloomberg L.P.|Bloomberg]]|date=29 July 2011|access-date=29 July 2011 }}</ref> The original fine to Mourinho was upheld along with a €20,000 fine assessed to Real Madrid for crowd trouble.<ref name="Mourinho appeal partially admitted"/>

The club traveled to [[Guangzhou]], China, directly from Leicester on 1 August,<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid land in China|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R8ZwtonfioU|last=McKee|first=Eric|publisher=[[Real Madrid TV]]|date=1 August 2011|access-date=3 August 2011 }}</ref> and signed a [[letter of intent]] the following day with [[Guangzhou Evergrande F.C.|Guangzhou Evergrande]] involving club cooperation, potential player exchanges, and the opening of the largest football academy in China.<ref>{{cite news|title=Real Madrid to help Chinese build the country's largest academy|url=http://news.xinhuanet.com/english2010/sports/2011-08/03/c_131026436.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120306234324/http://news.xinhuanet.com/english2010/sports/2011-08/03/c_131026436.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=6 March 2012|publisher=[[Xinhua News Agency|Xinhua]]|date=2 August 2011|access-date=3 August 2011 }}</ref> On 3 August, Real Madrid defeated [[Chinese Super League]] leaders Guangzhou Evergrande 7–1,<ref>{{cite web|script-title=zh:国际友谊赛 广州恒大1:7不敌皇家马德里 |url=http://www.gzevergrandefc.com/show_content.php?id=2326 |publisher=[[Guangzhou Evergrande F.C.|GZEvergrandefc.com]] |date=3 August 2011 |access-date=3 August 2011 |language=zh |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120326120024/http://www.gzevergrandefc.com/show_content.php?id=2326 |archive-date=26 March 2012 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Real thrash Chinese league leaders Guangzhou|url=https://www.google.com/hostednews/afp/article/ALeqM5jj-WO_UFBpn32RK0qfQulFJuKgkg?docId=CNG.05badf1c5a4779a5fba2bf67b2a83976.991|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130124204546/http://www.google.com/hostednews/afp/article/ALeqM5jj-WO_UFBpn32RK0qfQulFJuKgkg?docId=CNG.05badf1c5a4779a5fba2bf67b2a83976.991|url-status=dead|archive-date=24 January 2013|agency=[[Agence France-Presse]]|date=3 August 2011|access-date=3 August 2011 }}</ref> with goals from [[Sami Khedira]], Özil, Benzema twice, Ronaldo, Jesé, and [[Ángel Di María]].<ref>{{cite web|title=1–7 El Real Madrid se exhibe en Guangzhou|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gcRlQJv0GTA|last=Bernardo|first=Javier|publisher=[[Real Madrid TV]]|date=3 August 2011|access-date=3 August 2011|language=es }}</ref> The following day, [[Midfielder#Attacking midfielder|attacking midfielder]] [[Sergio Canales]] joined [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] on loan for two seasons with Valencia retaining a purchase option of €12&nbsp;million at the end of each season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Canales, cedido al Valencia|url=http://www.as.com/futbol/articulo/canales-cedido-valencia/20110804dasdasftb_41/Tes|last=Valle|first=Conrado|publisher=[[Diario AS|AS.com]]|date=4 August 2011|access-date=4 August 2011|language=es }}</ref> Real Madrid concluded their pre-season world tour with all victories on 6 August,<ref>{{cite web|title=Tianjin Teda 0–6 Real Madrid|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330063977422/noticia/Cronica/Tianjin_Teda_0-6_Real_Madrid.htm|last=Porrero|first=Fernando|publisher=[[Real Madrid C.F.]]|date=6 August 2011|access-date=6 August 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110915043816/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330063977422/noticia/Cronica/Tianjin_Teda_0-6_Real_Madrid.htm|archive-date=15 September 2011}}</ref> defeating [[Tianjin Teda F.C.|Tianjin Teda]] 6–0<ref>{{cite web|title=C罗控制力无敌本泽马梅开二度 泰达0:6不敌皇马|url=http://sports.enorth.com.cn/system/2011/08/06/007077113.shtml|publisher=[[Tianjin Teda F.C.|Enorth.com.cn]]|date=6 August 2011|access-date=6 August 2011|language=zh }}</ref> with goals from [[Kaká]], Di María, [[Gonzalo Higuaín]], Ronaldo and a double by Benzema.<ref name="GOALS: Tianjin Teda 0-6 Real Madrid">{{cite web|title=GOALS: Tianjin Teda 0–6 Real Madrid|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EX9ofYAjnU0|last=Hall|first=Andy|publisher=[[Real Madrid TV]]|date=6 August 2011|access-date=6 August 2011 }}</ref>

===August===
Real Madrid opened their competitive season with a 2–2 draw at home in the first leg of the [[2011 Supercopa de España]] against Barcelona on 14 August.<ref>{{cite news|title=Real, Barcelona locked at 2–2 in Supercup|url=http://www.bangkokpost.com/news/sports/251892/real-barcelona-locked-at-2-2-in-supercup|work=[[Bangkok Post]]|date=15 August 2011|access-date=14 August 2011 }}</ref> Özil scored after 13 minutes following an assist from Benzema, but goals from [[David Villa]] and [[Lionel Messi]] against the run of play gave Barcelona the lead at halftime.<ref>{{cite news|title=Soccer roundup: Barcelona, Real Madrid tie in first leg of Spanish Supercup|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2011/08/14/gIQA3EwsFJ_story.html|newspaper=The Washington Post|date=14 August 2011|access-date=15 August 2011|first=Paul|last=Tenorio}}</ref> [[Xabi Alonso]] shot through traffic during a corner sequence for the equalizer nine minutes into the second half.<ref>{{cite news|title=Real Madrid dominates Barcelona, but settle for Supercup draw|url=https://www.tsn.ca/soccer/story/?id=373804|agency=[[The Associated Press]]|publisher=[[The Sports Network]]|date=14 August 2011|access-date=14 August 2011 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=2–2: El fútbol no fue justo con el Real Madrid|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/1330064355471/noticia/Cronica/2-2:_El_futbol_no_fue_justo_con_el_Real_Madrid.htm|last=Porrero|first=Fernando|publisher=[[Real Madrid C.F.]]|date=15 August 2011|access-date=15 August 2011|language=es|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110815114633/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/1330064355471/noticia/Cronica/2-2%3A_El_futbol_no_fue_justo_con_el_Real_Madrid.htm|archive-date=15 August 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> Three days later in the return leg at [[Camp Nou]], Barcelona defeated Real Madrid 3–2 to win 5–4 on aggregate.<ref>{{cite web|title=Messi fires Barcelona to Super Cup win|url=http://english.aljazeera.net/sport/football/2011/08/201181835125105464.html|publisher=[[Al Jazeera English|AlJazeera.net]]|date=18 August 2011|access-date=9 September 2011 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Barcelona 3–2 Real Madrid|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330064621667/noticia/Cronica/Barcelona_3-2_Real_Madrid.htm|last=Porrero|first=Fernando|publisher=[[Real Madrid C.F.]]|date=17 August 2011|access-date=20 August 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110916032859/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330064621667/noticia/Cronica/Barcelona_3-2_Real_Madrid.htm|archive-date=16 September 2011}}</ref> [[Andrés Iniesta]] beat the [[Offside (association football)#Offside trap|offside trap]] and scored first for Barcelona, but Ronaldo redirected a cross to equalize five minutes later.<ref>{{cite news|title=Barcelona win Super Cup thriller thanks to Messi double|url=https://www.google.com/hostednews/afp/article/ALeqM5jSmbEsVMKgJcN3Y_WdE-F8oIwIQw?docId=CNG.6af0b2760c17cf45b85cc242fa5e2e58.ad1|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130125032757/http://www.google.com/hostednews/afp/article/ALeqM5jSmbEsVMKgJcN3Y_WdE-F8oIwIQw?docId=CNG.6af0b2760c17cf45b85cc242fa5e2e58.ad1|url-status=dead|archive-date=25 January 2013|last=Hanlon|first=Tim|agency=[[Agence France-Presse]]|date=17 August 2011|access-date=17 August 2011 }}</ref> Messi scored just before halftime following a failed clearance of a corner kick by Real Madrid and a subsequent backheel assist from [[Gerard Piqué]] to give Barcelona a 2–1 lead at halftime.<ref>{{cite web|title=Barcelona win Super Cup|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/330063?cc=5901|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120723222238/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/330063?cc=5901|url-status=dead|archive-date=23 July 2012|publisher=[[ESPNsoccernet]]|date=17 August 2011|access-date=17 August 2011}}</ref> Benzema leveled the score late in the second half following a scramble from a corner kick, but an [[Adriano (footballer, born 1984)|Adriano]] cross allowed Messi to score the winning goal in the 88th minute.<ref>{{cite news|title=Barcelona 3 Real Madrid 2; (agg 5–4): match report|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/players/lionel-messi/8707839/Barcelona-3-Real-Madrid-2-agg-5-4-match-report.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110818033226/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/players/lionel-messi/8707839/Barcelona-3-Real-Madrid-2-agg-5-4-match-report.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=18 August 2011|work=The Daily Telegraph|date=18 August 2011|access-date=17 August 2011|first1=Simon|last1=Talbot|first2=Jason|last2=Burt}}</ref> Marcelo received a straight red card in stoppage time for a tackle on [[Cesc Fàbregas]], creating an ensuing scuffle between the two sides that led to Mourinho confronting Barcelona assistant coach [[Tito Vilanova]] with a poke in the eye<ref>{{cite news|title=Jose Mourinho faces probe over Barcelona fracas|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14636124|work=BBC Sport|date=23 August 2011|access-date=23 August 2011 }}</ref> and expulsions of Villa and Özil.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.managingmadrid.com/2017/8/11/16128032/barcelona-real-madrid-spanish-supercup-2017-numbers|title=Remembering the 2011 Spanish Supercup between Real Madrid and Barcelona|author=Tim Higgins|date=11 August 2017 |publisher=[[SB Nation]]|access-date=11 August 2022|language=en}}</ref> Six days later, the [[Royal Spanish Football Federation]] opened disciplinary investigations against both Mourinho and Vilanova<ref>{{cite web|title=INCOACION EXPEDIENTES |url=http://www.rfef.es/FCKeditor/UserFiles/File/cursos_fundacion_ultimos/talentos/INCOACION%20EXPEDIENTES.pdf |publisher=[[Royal Spanish Football Federation|RFEF.es]] |date=23 August 2011 |access-date=23 August 2011 |language=es |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120323135003/http://www.rfef.es/FCKeditor/UserFiles/File/cursos_fundacion_ultimos/talentos/INCOACION%20EXPEDIENTES.pdf |archive-date=23 March 2012 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Comunicación pública de los acuerdos del juez unico de competición recaídos el 23 de agosto de 2011 |url=http://www.rfef.es/FCKeditor/UserFiles/File/cursos_fundacion_ultimos/talentos/NOTA%20SUPERCOPA.pdf |publisher=[[Royal Spanish Football Federation|RFEF.es]] |date=23 August 2011 |access-date=23 August 2011 |language=es |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120323135021/http://www.rfef.es/FCKeditor/UserFiles/File/cursos_fundacion_ultimos/talentos/NOTA%20SUPERCOPA.pdf |archive-date=23 March 2012 }}</ref> that could have potentially resulted in a 12-game suspension for Mourinho<ref>{{cite news|title=Mourinho apologizes to Madrid as lengthy ban looms|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/top-stories/Mourinho-apologizes-to-Madrid-as-lengthy-ban-looms/articleshow/9711198.cms|agency=[[The Associated Press]]|work=[[The Times of India]]|date=23 August 2011|access-date=23 August 2011 }}</ref> but instead suspended him for two future [[Supercopa de España]] matches and fined €600.<ref name="Resolución extraordinario Supercopa">{{cite web|title=Resolución extraordinario Supercopa |url=http://www.rfef.es/GetDoc?UniqueKeyValue=39887&ShowPath=false&Download=true |publisher=[[Royal Spanish Football Federation|RFEF.es]] |date=5 October 2011 |access-date=5 October 2011 |language=es |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120405172743/http://www.rfef.es/GetDoc?UniqueKeyValue=39887&ShowPath=false&Download=true |archive-date=5 April 2012 }}</ref> Real Madrid was additionally fined €180.<ref name="Resolución extraordinario Supercopa"/>

[[File:Partido Real Zaragoza Real Madrid 2011.jpg|thumb|left|Real Madrid players sporting their brand new black kits in an away match against Zaragoza]]
Real Madrid's [[La Liga]] campaign was scheduled to begin on 21 August at home against [[Athletic Bilbao]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Spanish football strike bites as first weekend falls victim|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2011/SPORT/football/08/19/football.spain.strike/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121025125051/http://edition.cnn.com/2011/SPORT/football/08/19/football.spain.strike/|url-status=dead|archive-date=25 October 2012|publisher=[[CNN International]]|date=19 August 2011|access-date=20 August 2011 }}</ref> but the [[Association of Spanish Footballers|Spanish Footballers' Association]], with representation from all 42 teams in the top two divisions,<ref>{{cite news|title=Talks resume to in Spanish players strike|url=https://af.reuters.com/article/sportsNews/idAFJOE77I06O20110819|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120927215903/http://af.reuters.com/article/sportsNews/idAFJOE77I06O20110819|url-status=dead|archive-date=27 September 2012|work=[[Reuters]]|date=19 August 2011|access-date=9 September 2011 }}</ref> unanimously elected to strike<ref>{{cite news|title=La Liga set for delayed start as Spanish players' union calls strike|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2011/aug/11/la-liga-spanish-union-strike|work=The Guardian|date=11 August 2011|access-date=20 August 2011 }}</ref> after failing to reach a [[collective bargaining]] agreement with the [[Liga de Fútbol Profesional]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Start of Primera Liga delayed|url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/sport/start-of-primera-liga-delayed-1.425252/|work=[[The National (Abu Dhabi)|The National]]|date=20 August 2011|access-date=20 August 2011 }}</ref> causing the postponement of the first weekend of fixtures.<ref>{{cite news |title=Spanish soccer strike goes on, latest talks fail |url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/soccer/2011-08-20-spanish-league-talks_n.htm |agency=[[The Associated Press]]|work=[[USA Today]]|date=20 August 2011 |access-date=9 August 2014}}</ref> The team won their seventh consecutive [[Trofeo Santiago Bernabéu|Santiago Bernabéu Trophy]], defeating Turkish [[Süper Lig]] side [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray]] on 24 August.<ref>{{cite news|title=Real Madrid ganó el Trofeo Bernabéu|url=https://espndeportes.espn.com/news/story?id=1363459&s=esp&type=story|agency=[[EFE]]|publisher=[[ESPN Deportes]]|date=24 August 2011|access-date=24 August 2011|language=es }}</ref> Before the match, Real Madrid officially presented their five new summer signings<ref>{{cite web|title=Sahin, Altintop, Callejon, Varane and Coentrao official presentation|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330064886109/noticia/Noticia/Sahin,_Altintop,_Callejon,_Varane_and_Coentrao_official_presentation.htm|last=O'Donnell|first=Michael J.|publisher=[[Real Madrid C.F.]]|date=24 August 2011|access-date=24 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110915030500/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330064886109/noticia/Noticia/Sahin,_Altintop,_Callejon,_Varane_and_Coentrao_official_presentation.htm|archive-date=15 September 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> and honored their three youth team players on the [[Spain national under-19 football team|Spanish under-19]] squad that won the [[2011 UEFA European Under-19 Championship|2011 UEFA European Under-19 Football Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Alex, Morata and Carvajal honoured in Santiago Bernabeu Trophy|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330064886374/noticia/Noticia/Alex,_Morata_and_Carvajal_honoured_in_Santiago_Bernabeu_Trophy.htm|last=O'Donnell|first=Michael J.|publisher=[[Real Madrid C.F.]]|date=24 August 2011|access-date=24 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110916021631/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330064886374/noticia/Noticia/Alex,_Morata_and_Carvajal_honoured_in_Santiago_Bernabeu_Trophy.htm|archive-date=16 September 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[Selçuk İnan]] scored early for Galatasaray from close range, but a pair of assists from man of the match Xabi Alonso<ref name="Man of the Match">{{cite web|title=Man of the Match|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330064962466/noticia/Noticia/Man_of_the_Match_2011-08-25.htm|last=O'Donnell|first=Michael J.|date=25 August 2011|access-date=24 August 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110916015946/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330064962466/noticia/Noticia/Man_of_the_Match_2011-08-25.htm|archive-date=16 September 2011}}</ref> to [[Sergio Ramos]] and Benzema led Real Madrid to a 2–1 victory in the annual friendly.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sergio Ramos and Benzema clinch Santiago Bernabeu Trophy for Whites|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bAT9kmYVGnA|last=McKee|first=Eric|publisher=[[Real Madrid TV]]|date=25 August 2011|access-date=27 August 2011 }}</ref> Real Madrid's La Liga season began ===January===
Real Madrid rallied to defeat [[Málaga CF|Málaga]] at home 3–2 in the first leg of the round of 16 in the Copa del Rey on 3 January.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real come from two down to beat big-spending Malaga|url=http://www.cnn.com/2012/01/03/sport/football/football-real-madrid-malaga/|publisher=[[CNN]]|date=3 January 2012|access-date=4 January 2012 }}</ref> Defenders [[Sergio Sánchez Ortega|Sergio Sánchez]] and [[Martín Demichelis]] converted headers from corners to give Málaga a 2–0 lead,<ref>{{cite web|title=Mourinho rocket sparks Real comeback|url=https://af.reuters.com/article/sportsNews/idAFJOE80301H20120104?sp=true|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160202031850/http://af.reuters.com/article/sportsNews/idAFJOE80301H20120104?sp=true|url-status=dead|archive-date=2 web|title=Real Madrid turn tie around|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11095/7409926/Copa-Del-Rey-round-up|last=Bate|first=Adam|publisher=[[Sky Sports|SkySports.com]]|date=3 January Malaga|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330076861716/noticia/Cronica/Real_Madrid_3-2_Malaga.htm|last=Porrero|first=Fernando|publisher=[[Real Madrid C.F.]]|date=3 January Barcelona|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330078332192/noticia/Cronica/Real_Madrid_1-2_Barcelona.htm|last=Porrero|first=Fernando|publisher=[[Real Madrid C.F.]]|date=18 January 2012|access-date=19 January 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120120195939/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330078332192/noticia/Cronica/Real_Madrid_1-2_Barcelona.htm|archive-date=20 Madrid|url=https://www.espn.com/sports/soccer/news/_/id/7476780/carles-puyol-eric-abidal-goals-give-barca-win-madrid|agency=[[The Associated Press]]|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=18 January 2012|access-date=19 January 2012 }}</ref> On 22 January, Real Madrid ended the first half of the season as league leaders with a five-point advantage after beating [[Athletic Bilbao]] at home 4–1. [[Fernando Llorente]] scored early for the visitors but Real Madrid eventually raced to clear 4–1 victory with two penalties from Ronaldo and goals from Marcelo and Callejón.<ref>{{cite news|title=Real Madrid 4–1 Athletic Bilbao: League leaders restore five-point advantage over Barcelona after coming from behind to secure victory|url=http://www.goal.com/en/match/74126/real-madrid-cf-vs-athletic-bilbao/report|publisher=Goal.com|date=23 January 2012|access-date=23 January 2012 }}</ref> On 25 January, Madrid was eliminated from Copa del Rey by Barcelona after a 2–2 draw at [[Camp Nou]]; Barcelona qualified 4–3 on aggregate. The home side was leading after the first half 2–0 with the goals from [[Pedro (footballer, born July 1987)|Pedro]] and [[Dani Alves]], despite Real Madrid being the dominating side. In the second half, Real Madrid leveled Barcelona with the goals from Ronaldo and Benzema.<ref>{{cite web|title=Barcelona 2–2 Real Madrid (4–3 Agg): Ronaldo & Benzema spark Blancos comeback but Pep Guardiola's men cling on to eliminate Copa del Rey holders|url=http://www.goal.com/en/match/73741/fc-barcelona-vs-real-madrid-cf/report|publisher=Goal.com|date=29 January 2012|access-date=27 January 2012 }}</ref> On 28 January, Real Madrid extended their lead in La Liga to seven points after beating [[Real Zaragoza]] home 3–1 while Barcelona could only conjure up a goalless draw away to [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Villarreal 0–0 Barcelona: Diego Lopez inspired for Yellow Submarine as champions fall seven points behind Real Madrid in La Liga title race|url=http://www.goal.com/en/match/63117/villarreal-vs-fc-barcelona/report|publisher=Goal.com|date=29 January 2012|access-date=29 January 2012|archive-date=31 January 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120131120822/http://www.goal.com/en/match/63117/villarreal-vs-fc-barcelona/report|url-status=dead}}</ref> Zaragoza took the lead in the 11th minute when [[Ángel Lafita]] scored for the visitors. Real Madrid, however, once again came from behind to finish with a comfortable win with goals from [[Kaká]], Ronaldo and Özil.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 3–1 Zaragoza: League leaders come from goal behind as Kaka, Ronaldo & Ozil strike to seal victory|url=http://www.goal.com/en/match/63122/real-madrid-cf-vs-zaragoza/report|publisher=Goal.com|date=28 January 2012|access-date=29 January 2012|archive-date=31 January 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120131123712/http://www.goal.com/en/match/63122/real-madrid-cf-vs-zaragoza/report|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===February===
On 4 February, Real Madrid started the month with a 0–1 away win over [[Getafe CF|Getafe]]. The lone goal, a header, was scored by [[Sergio Ramos]] in the first half.<ref>{{cite web|title=Getafe 0–1 Real Madrid: Jose Mourinho's men grind out valuable victory courtesy of first-half Sergio Ramos header|url=http://www.goal.com/en/match/63132/getafe-vs-real-madrid-cf/report|publisher=Goal.com|date=4 February 2012|access-date=4 February 2012 }}</ref> On 12 February, Madrid extended their lead in La Liga to ten points after winning 4–2 at home to [[Levante UD|Levante]], while Barcelona had lost the day before to [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]] in [[Pamplona]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Osasuna 3–2 Barcelona: Pep Guardiola's experimental side lose in Pamplona as La Liga starts to slip away|url=http://www.goal.com/en/match/63136/osasuna-vs-fc-barcelona/report|publisher=Goal.com|date=11 February 2012|access-date=13 February 2012 }}</ref> Levante opened the scoring with a header from [[Gustavo Cabral]]. The turning point came after a red card to [[Vicente Iborra]], giving away a penalty which was scored by [[Cristiano Ronaldo]]. Ronaldo then added two more goals, including a sumptuous third, before Levante pulled another back through [[Arouna Koné]]. [[Karim Benzema]] then curled home a fourth for Real to finish the scoring.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 4–2 Levante: Ronaldo nets superb hat-trick to send Jose Mourinho's side 10 points clear at summit of La Liga|url=http://www.goal.com/en/match/63143/real-madrid-cf-vs-levante/report|publisher=Goal.com|date=12 February 2012|access-date=13 February 2012 }}</ref> On 18 February, Real Madrid continued their good form in La Liga by beating [[Racing de Santander]] at the Bernabéu 4–0. Benzema netted a brace and Ronaldo and [[Ángel Di María]] each scored one goal in the comfortable win. Racing played over half of the game with only ten men after [[Domingo Cisma]] received a second yellow card for his second handball of the game and was sent off.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 4–0 Racing Santander: Ronaldo, Benzema & Di Maria on target in easy win for Mourinho's men|url=http://www.goal.com/en/match/63153/real-madrid-cf-vs-racing/report|publisher=Goal.com|date=18 February 2012|access-date=19 February 2012 }}</ref> On 21 February, Real Madrid drew 1–1 with [[PFC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] in the away leg of their Champions League round of 16 tie. The game, played in snowy conditions in Moscow, was led by Madrid for the majority of the match with a goal from Ronaldo, but a last-minute equalizer by [[Pontus Wernbloom]] denied the victory for the visitors.<ref>{{cite web|title=CSKA Moscow 1–1 Real Madrid: Stoppage-time equaliser from Wernbloom cancels out Ronaldo opener and gives Russians battling draw|url=http://www.goal.com/en/match/71882/pfc-cska-moskva-vs-real-madrid-cf/report|publisher=Goal.com|date=21 February 2012|access-date=21 February 2012 }}</ref> On 26 February, Real Madrid defeated city rival [[Rayo Vallecano]] at the [[Campo de Fútbol de Vallecas]] by a score of 0–1. The only goal of the game, a back-heel effort by Cristiano Ronaldo, was eventually enough for the visitors to go home with the three points in their pocket.<ref>{{cite web|title=Taconazo de oro de Ronaldo|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo/1330086977249/noticia/Cronica/0-1:_Taconazo_de_oro_de_Ronaldo.htm|publisher=[[Real Madrid C.F.]]|date=26 February 2012|access-date=26 February 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120229043156/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo/1330086977249/noticia/Cronica/0-1:_Taconazo_de_oro_de_Ronaldo.htm|archive-date=29 February 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===March===
On 4 March, Real Madrid extended their streak of wins in La Liga to ten games by beating [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] at home 5–0. [[Cristiano Ronaldo]], [[Sami Khedira]] and [[Kaká]] all scored in the impressive win, as did [[Gonzalo Higuaín]], who scored twice.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/match/63172/real-madrid-cf-vs-espanyol/report|publisher=Goal.com|date=4 March 2012 |title=Real Madrid 5–0 Espanyol |access-date=9 August 2014}}</ref> On 10 March, Real Madrid became the first team in the history of La Liga to win ten consecutive away games after beating [[Real Betis]] 2–3 at the [[Estadio Benito Villamarín]]. The home team started well after [[Jorge Molina Vidal|Jorge Molina]] scored early, but Higuaín equalized just over ten minutes later. In the second half, Madrid took the lead with a Ronaldo goal, but Betis equalized only a few minutes later with a strike from [[Jefferson Montero]]. Ronaldo, however, scored his second of the night later on which turned out to be the winning goal and guaranteed the full three points for the whites.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/match/63182/betis-vs-real-madrid-cf/report|publisher=Goal.com|date=11 March 2012 |title=Betis 2–3 Real Madrid |access-date=9 August 2014}}</ref> Real Madrid qualified for the quarter-finals of the Champions League on 14 March by beating [[PFC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] at home by a score of 4–1, progressing 5–2 on aggregate. Ronaldo netted a brace while Higuaín and [[Karim Benzema]] both scored one in the victory, while the lone goal from CSKA was scored by [[Zoran Tošić]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/match/71890/real-madrid-cf-vs-pfc-cska-moskva/report|publisher=Goal.com|date=14 March 2012 |title=Real Madrid 4–1 CSKA Moscow |access-date=9 August 2014}}</ref> On 18 March, Real Madrid tied against [[Málaga CF|Málaga]] at the Bernabéu 1–1 after an injury time free kick by [[Santi Cazorla]]. Real Madrid's only goal was scored by Benzema.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/la-liga/2011-2012/live-real-madrid-malaga-cf_mtc459036/live.shtml|title = Real Madrid - Málaga CF live - 18 March 2012|date = 18 March 2012}}</ref> On 21 March, Real Madrid drew again 1–1, this time against [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] on the road, with Ronaldo and [[Marcos Senna]] scoring the goals. After back-to-back draws, Real Madrid was on an advantage of just six points ahead of rivals Barcelona. In the controversial game, Mourinho was expelled from the match as was fitness trainer Rui Faria for the third time in his season. The referee gave [[Sergio Ramos]] a second yellow card for a tough challenge on [[Nilmar]] and gave direct red to Özil for sarcastically applauding his decision.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/la-liga/2011-2012/live-villarreal-cf-real-madrid_mtc459030/live.shtml|title = Villarreal CF - Real Madrid live - 21 March 2012|date = 21 March 2012}}</ref> [[Pepe (footballer, born 1983)|Pepe]] was also booked after the game for insulting the referee, which led to a two-game suspension for him. On 24 March, Real Madrid beat [[Real Sociedad]] 5–1, with two goals each from Ronaldo and Benzema and a single goal for Higuaín.<ref>{{cite web| url-status = live| archive-url = https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211205/0coRWKriYMI| archive-date = 2021-12-05| url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0coRWKriYMI| title = Resumen de Real Madrid vs Real Sociedad (5-1) 2011/2012 | website=[[YouTube]]}}{{cbignore}}</ref> Ronaldo averaged 1.01 goals per game by having 100 goals scored in La Liga that day. On the following week, on 27 March, Real Madrid continued their good form in the Champions League quarter-finals first leg by defeating opponent [[APOEL FC|APOEL]] in Cyprus 0–3.<ref name="Real Madrid 5-2 Apoel Agg 8-2">{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/17600978|title = Real Madrid 5-2 Apoel (Agg 8-2)|work = BBC Sport}}</ref> Benzema scored a header from a pass from Kaká, who then scored the second one; Benzema closed the game by scoring the third goal from an Özil assist.<ref name="Real Madrid 5-2 Apoel Agg 8-2"/> On the last day of the month, Real Madrid beat [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]] away, 1–5. Benzema scored a stupendous volley goal and Ronaldo equally great 36-yard long range shot at goal.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/soccer/2012/3/31/2916692/real-madrid-vs-osasuna-final-score-report-2012-la-liga|title = Osasuna Vs. Real Madrid, 2012 la Liga: Los Blancos Coast to 5-1 Win|date = 31 March 2012}}</ref> It was overall Ronaldo's night, since he also scored another goal, a free kick that was deflected, and assisted two other goals. Higuaín was the third player who got his name on the scoresheet, scoring twice. His last goal was the 100th goal for Madrid in La Liga this season.<ref name="auto"/>

===April===
[[File:Camp Nou, partit Futbol Club Barcelona - Reial Madrid (abril 2012) - panoramio.jpg|thumb|left|Barcelona and Real Madrid prior to the kick-off of the league's decisive ''El Clásico'']]
The month started with a 5–2 victory over APOEL in the second leg of the Champions League quarter-finals on 4 April, giving an aggregate score 8–2 as ''Los Blancos'' advanced to the semi-finals against final hosts [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]]. Real Madrid was resting some of their usual starters, but still managed to score five goals overall. [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] netted a brace and [[Kaká]], [[José Callejón]] and [[Ángel Di María]] each scored one in the victory, while APOEL's goals were scored by [[Gustavo Manduca]] and [[Esteban Solari]], the latter scoring a penalty given to the Cypriots after [[Hamit Altıntop]]'s foul in the penalty area.<ref name="Real Madrid 5-2 Apoel Agg 8-2"/> On 8 April, Real Madrid had a goalless draw against [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] in La Liga, leaving them only four points ahead of Barcelona.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.whoscored.com/Matches/523343/Preview/Spain-La-Liga-2011-2012-Real-Madrid-Valencia|title=Real Madrid 0 : Valencia 0|website=Whoscored.com|access-date=5 July 2022}}</ref> Three days later, on 11 April, Real Madrid beat [[Atlético Madrid]] in an away game 1–4. Cristiano Ronaldo scored a hat-trick, including two astonishing goals, and assisted Callejón to score the fourth goal to close the game. Atlético's only goal was netted by [[Radamel Falcao]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/soccer/2012/4/11/2942136/real-madrid-vs-atletico-madrid-final-score-report-2012-la-liga-cristiano-ronaldo|title = Atletico Madrid Vs. Real Madrid, 2012 la Liga: Final Score, Los Blancos Win 4-1|date = 11 April 2012}}</ref> On 14 April, Real Madrid beat [[Sporting de Gijón]] home 3–1 with goals from Higuaín, Ronaldo and Benzema. Sporting's only goal was a penalty given to them after a handball from [[Sergio Ramos]] in the box, which was scored by [[Miguel de las Cuevas]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/soccer/2012/4/14/2948670/real-madrid-vs-sporting-gijon-2012-la-liga-final-score|title = Real Madrid Vs. Sporting Gijon, 2012 la Liga: Final Score 3-1 Real as Hosts Survive Scare|date = 14 April 2012}}</ref> On 17 April, Real Madrid lost to Bayern Munich away at the [[Allianz Arena]] 2–1 in the first leg of the Champions League semi-finals. [[Franck Ribéry]] and [[Mario Gómez]] scored for Bayern (the latter in the closing moments of the game), while [[Mesut Özil]] netted Madrid's lone goal.<ref name="R Madrid 2-1 B Munich Agg 3-3">{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/17832633|title = R Madrid 2-1 B Munich (Agg 3-3)|work = BBC Sport}}</ref> On 21 April, Real Madrid defeated Barcelona in ''El Clásico'' at [[Camp Nou]] 1–2, extending their lead in La Liga to seven points with only four matches left, which all but decided the league title. [[Sami Khedira]] opened the scoring from a corner kick in the 17th minute which broke the world record for the most goals scored in a single domestic league season, with 107. [[Alexis Sánchez]] equalized in the second half in the 70th minute, but only a few minutes later, Özil assisted and Ronaldo scored the winning goal of the game by shooting the ball over [[Víctor Valdés]] into the net. Madrid completely outplayed Barça's "unbeatable" dream team, neutralizing their [[tiki-taka]] style, and put out a statement victory which was widely viewed as a sign of changes in the existing football hierarchy, with ''Los Blancos'' overtaking Barcelona as a pre-eminent power both in Spain and Europe.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/17801506|title = Barcelona 1-2 Real Madrid|work = BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=El Clasico 2012: Barcelona vs. Real Madrid Establishes Itself as Best Rivalry|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1154642-el-clasico-2012-barcelona-vs-real-madrid-establishes-itself-as-best-rivalry|work=[[Bleacher Report]]}}</ref> On 25 April, in the second leg of the Champions League semi-finals against Bayern Munich, Cristiano Ronaldo initially put Madrid up 2–0, but former Madrid player [[Arjen Robben]] netted an away goal back for Bayern with a penalty. The match ended 2–1 after extra time and as both sides were tied 3–3, it went to a shootout. During penalties, [[Iker Casillas]] made two saves but Ronaldo, Kaká and Ramos failed to convert their spot kicks and Madrid lost 3–1, bowing out of the Champions League in a heartbreaking fashion.<ref name="R Madrid 2-1 B Munich Agg 3-3"/> The Champions League setback did not break Madrid's spirit, however, as the team went on to crush [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] 3–0 just four days after the UCL semi-finals heartbreak. Ronaldo opened the scoring and Benzema then added a brace.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/la-liga/2011-2012/live-real-madrid-sevilla-fc_mtc458968/live.shtml|title = Real Madrid - Sevilla FC live - 29 April 2012|date = 29 April 2012}}</ref>

===May===
[[File:La Liga de los 100 (7197707348).jpg|thumb|right|Madrid players celebrate their record-breaking league title after a final day victory over Mallorca]]
On 2 May 2012, ''Los Blancos'' defeated [[Athletic Bilbao]] 3–0 in an away game to be crowned champions of Spain after a four-year wait. Higuaín, Özil, and Ronaldo scored as Madrid won La Liga with two games to spare.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/soccer/2012/5/2/2994926/real-madrid-vs-athletic-bilbao-2012-la-liga-champions-final-score-report|title = Athletic Bilbao Vs. Real Madrid, 2012 la Liga: Los Merengues Are Champions|date = 2 May 2012}}</ref> That wasn't it however, as the team clearly targeted to achieve a record 100 points in a season. Madrid went on to beat [[Granada CF|Granada]] away three days later in a dramatic game that saw the home team score early, with Ronaldo equalizing in the 81st minute through a penalty, and Real clinching the victory in injury time, courtesy of an own goal. Two Granada players were sent off after the final whistle after a brawl involving the teams.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com.au/football/report?gameId=325205|title = Granada vs. Real Madrid - Football Match Report - May 5, 2012 - ESPN}}</ref> The final game of the season was against [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]] at the Bernabéu. Prior to that game, ''Madridistas'' had 97 points, meaning that they had to win to become the ''Centurions''. Real did just that by triumphing 4–1 with goals coming from Ronaldo, Benzema, and Özil (2). The team reached the 100-point mark and set numerous records in the process.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.managingmadrid.com/2012/5/13/3018223/real-madrid-vs-mallorca-la-liga-2012-match-recap-the-team-of-100|title = Real Madrid Vs. Mallorca, La Liga 2012 Match Recap: 100 Points|date = 13 May 2012}}</ref> Overall, La Liga title was a sufficient consolation for a heartbreak in the Champions League semi-finals against Bayern and earlier defeats to Barça in the Supercopa and Copa del Rey.
